rounds.text: Anjani Finance Ltd trades at a highly discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.60x based on a share price of ₹ 8.99 and a book value of ₹ 15.1 [E2]. Furthermore, the company's valuation compares favourably against sector benchmarks, showing a price-to-earnings multiple of 19.5x relative to the sector benchmark of 20.02x [E6] and a price-to-book of 0.86x against the sector benchmark of 1.35x [E7]. Operational efficiency is notably strong, with a return on assets (ROA) of 4.43% that substantially outperforms the sector benchmark of 1.83% [E8]. Additionally, the stock sits near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 21% of the way up from its low, leaving substantial room for recovery from its micro-cap valuation of ₹ 9.12 Cr [E3, E5]. Conceded: E1, E4, E12, E13, E26, E27, E28, E29, E57, E61.

Anjani Finance Ltd trades at an expensive trailing price-to-earnings multiple of 57 based on filed statements [E1], which is hard to justify given the deeply depressed returns generated by the business. The company delivers a negligible return on capital employed of just 1.4% [E12] and a meager return on equity of 1.1% [E13]. This poor profitability is not a temporary blip but a structural feature, evidenced by a stagnant 10-year median return on equity of 3% that has further deteriorated to a median of 1% over the last year [E26, E29]. These chronically low returns led the scanX signal engine and filed statements to formally flag the low 3-year average ROE of 2.18% as a negative indicator [E57, E61]. Furthermore, shareholders receive zero income for tying up capital, as demonstrated by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], while the stock languishes near the bottom of its annual spectrum at only 21% of the way up its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits below unity at 0.60x alongside peer comparisons showing a P/E of 19.5x and an ROA of 4.43% [E2, E6, E8].

Conceded: the trailing P/E is 57 [E1] and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. However, the bear's focus on the P/E ignores the much more moderate P/E of 19.5x relative to the sector benchmark of 20.02x [E6]. The critique of historical returns overlooks that the company's return on assets of 4.43% substantially outperforms the sector benchmark of 1.83% [E8]. While the bear highlights low single-digit ROE figures [E13, E29, E57, E61], the stock trades at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.60x according to filed statements [E2], and 0.86x against a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E7]. Finally, the claim that the stock languishes at 21% of its 52-week range [E5] simply describes a micro-cap security priced at ₹ 8.99 with a market capitalisation of ₹ 9.12 Cr [E3] that is primed for asset-based revaluation rather than structural abandonment.

Conceded: the data provider lists a P/E of 19.5x against a sector benchmark of 20.02x [E6], and a P/B of 0.86x against a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E7]. However, filed statements confirm a trailing P/E of 57 [E1], proving that the headline valuation is heavily inflated depending on the reporting source. Conceded: the company displays an ROA of 4.43% against a sector benchmark of 1.83% [E8]. Despite this asset return, the business generates an ROCE of just 1.4% [E12] and a 10-year median ROE of only 3% [E26], which has further deteriorated to a 3-year median of 2% [E28] and a 1-year ROE of 1% [E29]. The bull's characterization of the ₹ 9.12 Cr micro-cap [E3] as primed for asset-based revaluation ignores that this depressed valuation—sitting at 21% of its 52-week range [E5] with a 0.00% dividend yield [E4]—is fully justified by persistent low-return performance flagged directly in filed statements [E57, E61].
